trickyParts: The per-object tally reaches the object's own keys and never its subtree. A nested text object, and each element of a fields array, is an object of its own with a tally of its own; a subtree-wide tally would drop a nested block's word for matching a title above it, which is the same defect class one level down.
At most one string is yielded per display name, so a tally holds nine at the most and is a slice scanned straight through rather than a map.
takeOwn still delivers the own text as one piece and then records it and each of its non-blank lines; take compares against nothing else, so no piece gathered from the tree ever suppresses another.
The committed claude-envoy plugin bundle mirrors skills/, and the required check-dist step fails if the skill file is edited without rebuilding it.
